diagnostic_evidence.quote: Note that the unique entries of $R_k$ in its first column, are evaluated using this corresponding column of $W\Tilde{A}$ i.e. $R_k\hat{e}_1 = (D^k)^{-1}(W\Tilde{A})^{(k)}$, as in step-4 of this algorithm.

issues.failure_explanation: With U = W\tilde{A} whose columns are the cycle diagonals Lambda_j (appendix example), U(k,j) = (1/sqrt(n)) sum_q Lambda_j(q,q) omega^{-kq}. The first column of the k-th circulant component is therefore R_k(j,0) = (omega^{kj}/sqrt(n)) U(k,j) — built from ROW k of U twisted by D^k, exactly matching the mean-of-cycle formula of thm:added-2. Step 4 instead uses COLUMN k of U with the inverse phase (D^k)^{-1}, giving a different vector: e.g. for n=2, A=[[1,2],[3,4]] the true R_1(:,0) = (-3/2, 1/2)^T while the stated formula yields (5,1)^T (unnormalized FFT), not even proportional. So as written the algorithm does not output the circulant components R_j (j >= 1), contradicting the paper's own thm:added-2 and breaking its input-output contract.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace Step 4 with the row-based extraction R[j] <- (1/sqrt(n)) D^j (row j of U)^T (up to FFT normalization), equivalently implement the mean formula of thm:added-2.
issues.overall_effect: The algorithm returns wrong R_j for j >= 1; consequently the weights T_A[i] = ||R_A[i]||_2 and the truncated matrices in Steps 2-4 of algo:cd_matrix_multiplication would also be built from incorrect components. The claimed O(n^2 log n) cost is unaffected.
issues.title: FFT circulant-decomposition algorithm extracts the wrong vector as the first column of R_k
issues.why_classification: A one-line local correction whose correct form is forced by the paper's own thm:added-2; no new lemma, no change to complexity, methods, or results.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: W\bm l_k \circ W(D^k\bm b) = W \bm l_k \circ WD^kW^{*}W\bm b =  W\bm l_k \circ C^kW\bm b

issues.failure_explanation: The paper's own derivation shows the Fourier-domain factor must be W l_t, the FFT of the first column l_t of the circulant R_t (l_t mixes all cycles at frequency t: l_t(j) = omega^{jt} rho_{j,t}). But Algorithm algo:circulant_decomposition_fft defines the output L as the raw cycle diagonals Lambda_t, so Step 5 multiplies by Lambda_t; as written it computes W^* sum_t diag(Lambda_t) C^t W B = sum_t circ(W^* Lambda_t) D^t B, which is not \tilde{A}B = sum_t R_t D^t B. The same defect appears in the second line, which uses L_B[t] for the Delta A \tilde{B} term. The algorithm as written therefore does not deliver the claimed first-order approximation \tilde{A}B + Delta A \tilde{B} of eq:first_order_expansion.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace L_A[t] by the Hadamard factor FFT(R_A[t]) (and analogously use the right-multiplication kernel, the FFT of the reversed first column of R_t, in the second line), exactly as derived in the preceding prose.
issues.overall_effect: The central circulant-decomposition multiplication algorithm, as written, computes a different product than the advertised first-order approximation; its guarantee (approximate AB in O(n^2 log n)) fails without correction.
issues.title: Fourier-domain products in the CD multiplication algorithm use the cycle diagonals Lambda_t instead of the FFT of the circulant first column
issues.why_classification: Local one-line-per-product correction; the correct left-multiplication factor is already derived in the paper; complexity and all stated results are unchanged.

issues.title: Concentration corollary states exponent constant 48 while its proof derives 96
issues.why_classification: Single forced correction with no effect on any downstream qualitative use; every substantive claim survives.

issues.failure_explanation: As written the statement asserts an exact equality between a deterministic expectation and the random quantity (3/4)||A||_F||B||_F, which is false and ill-defined: for m=n=p=1, E[xy] = a^2/4 while (3/4)xy is random with mean 3a^2/16; and the exact ratio computed in the proof is 1/n + 9(n-1)/(16n), equal to 9/16 only as n -> infinity. The proof establishes only E||AB||_F^2 approximately (9/16) E||A||_F^2 E||B||_F^2 for large n, then passes to E[S] approximately sqrt(E[S^2]) and replaces the expected norms by the known norms without any concentration argument; independence of all entries is used but never stated as a hypothesis.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restate the theorem as the asymptotic statement: for independent entries, E||AB||_F^2 / (E||A||_F^2 E||B||_F^2) -> 9/16 and E||AB||_F approximately (3/4)||A||_F||B||_F for n >> 1, matching the proof's final line.

issues.title: Theorem states exact identity E||AB||_F = (3/4)||A||_F||B||_F while the proof only establishes an asymptotic approximation
issues.why_classification: The supported approximate statement is already what the proof delivers and what the paper uses; restating requires no new substantive argument and loses nothing used downstream.

issues.failure_explanation: For Haar Q (the complex case used, since E|Q_ij|^4 = 2/(n(n+1))), the cross-moment E|Q_ij|^2|Q_kl|^2 equals 1/(n(n+1)) only when the distinct pairs share a row or a column; for i != k and j != l the correct value is 1/(n^2-1). Applying 1/(n(n+1)) to every pair (i,j) != (k,l) makes the case split invalid and the resulting formula false: for D_1 = D_2 = I, S = ||Q||_F^2 = n deterministically so E[S^2] = n^2, but the lemma gives (n^4+n)/(n(n+1)) = n(n^2+1)/(n+1) != n^2 (n=2: 10/3 != 4). The correct value (Weingarten) is [n(alpha_1^2 alpha_2^2 + beta_1 beta_2) - beta_1 alpha_2^2 - alpha_1^2 beta_2]/(n(n^2-1)). Consequently lem:added-2's 'variance' is negative in concrete cases (D_1=D_2=I gives -n(n-1)/(n+1) instead of 0, and it is generically negative for large n), and the final delta-method display yields E[sqrt(S)] > sqrt(E[S]) (the correction +1/(8(n+1)) dominates), contradicting Jensen's inequality E[sqrt(S)] <= sqrt(E[S]).

failure_location.quote: Now using the fact that for Haar distributed matrices we have $\mathbf{E}[|Q_{i,j}|^4]  = \frac{2}{n(n+1)}$ and $\mathbf{E}[|Q_{i,j}|^2 |Q_{k,l}|^2]  = \frac{1}{n(n+1)}$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Recompute E[S^2] splitting into the cases (i,j)=(k,l), shared row or column, and distinct rows and columns, using the correct Weingarten moments 2/(n(n+1)), 1/(n(n+1)), 1/(n^2-1); restate lem:added-1 and lem:added-2 with the correct formulas and recompute the delta-method correction, which then has the correct (negative) sign.
issues.overall_effect: The appendix's exact second-moment and variance formulas and the concluding E[sqrt(S)] expansion are false as stated; quantitative support for the main-text heuristic E||AB||_F approximately sqrt(E||AB||_F^2) is undermined, although the qualitative conclusion (relative variance -> 0, E[sqrt(S)] approximately sqrt(E[S])) remains valid and is independently supported by th:concentrationprob.
issues.title: Wrong Haar fourth-moment formula invalidates the appendix's E[S^2] and variance formulas
issues.why_classification: The stated formulas are false and must be replaced via a contained but nontrivial moment recomputation; no global proof architecture changes and the qualitative conclusion survives, so this exceeds a local fix but causes no major loss.
